item.title: Attaching Everpure Cloud Azure Native Storage to Azure Red Hat OpenShift
item.description: Previously, I deployed an Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) cluster with Terraform , into an existing VNet with its own dedicated subnets. That gives you a working cluster, but the persistent storage still has to come from somewhere. This time I am provisioning Everpure Cloud Azure Native volume groups for the cluster, and pulling the iSCSI connection parameters back out of the API, which is the piece this post is really about.

item.title: Provisioning Azure Resources with the azapi Terraform Provider
item.description:
Are you looking for a way to use Terraform to provision Azure resources that aren’t in the azurerm provider yet? The azapi provider talks directly to the Azure ARM REST API, which means you can manage any resource type the moment it’s available, without waiting on a provider update.

In this post, I’ll walk you through finding the resource type and API version, writing an azapi_resource block, reading outputs, and calling resource actions. I’ll use Azure Monitor Workspace and Azure Managed Grafana as the examples, which together give you a complete managed observability stack.
